findings.body:
**Return one JSON artifact from every CLI path.**

In `apps/crq-python/crq_repair.py:1279`, explicit job processing discards the result without calling `write_result`. The automatic drain also emits no JSON when the optional triage phase does not run, including an empty-inbox pass. A caller cannot parse a result from these successful invocations.

Make `main` own result emission. Return structured outcomes from job processing and draining, and emit exactly one artifact, including for no-work and refusal outcomes.

As per coding guidelines, I1 requires: “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Return one JSON artifact from every CLI path.

findings.body:
**Persist existing artifact entries before returning success.**

In `apps/crq-python/review_ledger.py:400`, a matching file bypasses all synchronization. If `atomic` replaces the file and its directory fsync fails, a retry returns this file without persisting its directory entry. A later system crash can then lose an artifact that the retry reported as durable.

Synchronize the artifact directory on this path too. `put_file` already handles this retry case at Lines 441–444.
findings.title: Persist existing artifact entries before returning success.

findings.body:
**Persist ancestor entries when retrying directory creation.**

In `apps/crq-python/review_ledger.py:366`, an existing target causes synchronization of only its immediate parent.

For example, create `base/outbox/pending` when only `base` exists. If synchronization of `base` fails, a retry synchronizes `outbox` but not `base`. Subsequent event writes can succeed while the `outbox` entry remains unpersisted. A later system crash can lose those events.

Make recovery persist the ancestor entries too, not only entries discovered as missing during the current call.
findings.title: Persist ancestor entries when retrying directory creation.

findings.body:
**Let completed manual and agent reports pass the vendor-credit check.**

`validate_provenance` accepts a manual or agent review with `outcome: "completed"` when completion evidence and verified scope are present. `validate` then raises `IntegrityError` at `review_ledger.py:226-227` because `creditable()` returns `False` for every non-vendor producer. The provenance check and the ingestion check therefore disagree, and records that pass the first fail the second. The module comment at lines 260-261 says these completions cannot earn vendor credit. It does not say they must be rejected. Limit the credit check to reports that are not manual or agent reports. Those reports keep their credit exclusion through `creditable()`.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-        if p["outcome"] == "completed" and not creditable(value):
+        if p["outcome"] == "completed" and not report_producer(value) and not creditable(value):
             raise IntegrityError("completed review lacks authenticated scoped completion")
```

</details>
findings.title: Let completed manual and agent reports pass the vendor-credit check.
